The task: adjust left rail label so it doesn't crowd the big title. The rail-label is rotated -90deg with transform-origin left top at left:44px, top:520px. Rotated text extends upward from the origin point... Actually rotate(-90deg) with origin left top: the text line goes from (44, 520) upward. Its width (360px) becomes vertical extent, and height 22px becomes horizontal extent extending to the left? Let's think: rotate(-90deg) rotates counterclockwise. A point (x,0) in local coords maps to (0,-x) in parent coords → upward. The element's height (22px) extends downward in local y → after rotation, local +y maps to (+y, 0)... rotation by -90: (x,y) → (x cos(-90) - y sin(-90), x sin(-90) + y cos(-90)) = (0*x + y, -x + 0) = (y, -x). So local (x,y) → (y, -x). So local y (height) becomes horizontal +x direction, i.e., to the right. So the text box occupies horizontal range from x=44 to x=44+22=66 relative... and vertically from 520 up to 520-360=160.

The title h1 starts at left 96px. So the rail label's right edge is at 44+22=66px, which is 30px gap to 96px. But text glyphs may be positioned... The rotated text baseline etc. Actually the visible text could extend. Hmm, but the collision: the rotated text spans vertically 160–520. Title "第一天" is at top 168 + ... let's compute: content top 168, left padding-top 26 → left column starts at 194. eyebrow ~ font 15px, then h1 margin-top 20. So h1 starts around 194+ (15*? line height) ~ 194+ ~20 + 20 = ~234. Title font 136px, so spans 234 to ~373. The rotated label spans y from 160 to 520 at x 44–66. Title starts x=96. Gap 30px — tight-ish given letter-spacing on rotated text? Actually the text width 360px for "DAY 01 · 第一天 · 步行与摄影" with letterspacing 5.1px — the text may be wider than 360px, overflowing, but overflow visible; it extends further up (beyond 160).

The fix: move label right and/or shorten. Instruction: "仅调整左边距：将左边缘竖排小字向右移动或缩短，与超大标题左侧笔画之间留出明显安全间距". So we should move it right (increase left) and/or shorten the text. But also "文字内容与其他元素不变" — text content unchanged. So keep text but move right? Hmm—if we move it right, it gets closer to the title... Wait, moving right increases x, closer to title at 96. That's wrong. Wait—rotate with origin left top: local y maps to +x. So moving right moves it toward title. That's counterproductive.

Hmm, maybe the actual visual: the label is at left 44, its box extends right to 66. The title starts at 96. So gap is 30px. To increase the gap, we should move the label LEFT (decrease left) — but left rule is at 60px, ticks at 54. Hmm, moving left would cross the rule.

Alternatively the issue may be that the rotated text with letter-spacing... Actually wait, maybe the glyphs render beyond the box because of the line-height (22px height for 13px font — fine).

Hmm. The instruction says move right or shorten. Maybe the actual perceived crowding: the label's rotated text as rendered actually extends to x≈66 but visually the left column's h1 at 96... 30px gap for a 136px title — that appears crowded. To get "明显安全间距", better to reduce the vertical extent... no.

Best approach: shrink the label so its horizontal footprint is smaller (it already is 22px tall box). Options:
1. Move the label left so the gap grows: e.g. left: 30px with the left rule at 60... it would overlap the rule line. Hmm, but the label is text; overlapping the vertical rule could be fine? Not great.

Alternative: relocate the label to a different vertical position where there's no title — but instruction says only adjust left margin.

Actually maybe a cleaner approach: change the transform origin / position so text sits in left margin at x ~ 16–38 and rotate about... But the left rule at 60px would be crossed.

Hmm, let's reconsider: Maybe simply move label right is what's asked because the user perceives the text near x=44-66 and title at 96... moving right would reduce gap. Unless the user's mental model is different. The instruction is "向右移动或缩短" — move right OR shorten. Perhaps shortening means making the rotated text shorter (less tall) so it doesn't extend into the title's vertical band... that doesn't help horizontal crowding either.

Hmm, maybe the real problem: with letter-spacing 5.1px, text is wider than 360px, so it overflows the box upward — vertically. Not horizontal.

Let me reconsider the geometry more carefully. Rotate(-90) about left top, element at left:44, top:520, width 360, height 22.

Local point (0,0) → parent (44+0, 520-0) = (44,520). Local (x,y) → parent (44+y, 520-x). So local y from 0..22 → parent x from 44..66. Local x from 0..360 → parent y 520..160. Good, as I said.

Text baseline: for 13px font in 22px line box, baseline ~ y≈16 in local, → parent x ≈ 60. Text ascenders go up in local y decreasing → parent x decreasing. So glyph tops at local y≈5 → x≈49, descenders at local y≈19 → x≈63. So glyphs occupy x 49–63, right at the left rule (x=60). Slight overlap with the rule line. That's existing.

Gap to title: 96 - 63 = 33px. For a 136px serif title, 33px is small, appears crowded.

To increase gap while keeping the rule, one could move the label left: left: 20px → glyphs at x 25–39, gap 57px, but then it's left of the... left rule at 60 — actually it'd be to the left of the rule which is fine visually? The straightforward implementation: reduce the label's horizontal footprint by reducing font/height and shifting, or move the label to a position with more clearance.
